family.description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the Impact proteins. The Impact protein is a translational regulator that ensures constant high levels of translation under amino acid starvation. It acts by interacting with Gcn1/Gcn1L1, thereby preventing activation of Gcn2 protein kinases (EIF2AK1 to 4) and subsequent down-regulation of protein synthesis [[cite:PUB00161305],[cite:PUB00158485]]. It is evolutionary conserved from eukaryotes to archaea [[cite:PUB00046141]].
family.name: Impact N-terminal domain

history.description: Researched Sattlegger 2011 Methods and fragment results; visually inspected Figures 2 and 5. Mapped cited GI 6319904 to P25637/NP_009985.1 and distinguished PF01205 144-251 from RWD 6-108 and the unrelated PCI8 YIH1 synonym. Added three indirect observed effects with separate H1511 phosphorylation, H1511 growth and ESY11001b growth contexts, minimal evidence and an open domain/coverage discussion. No isolated-domain inhibition, independent review or publication is claimed.

causal_graphs.context: Galactose-induced exponential cultures are treated with 10 mM 3AT for 1 h before harvesting. Immunoblots measure Ser51-phosphorylated eIF2alpha relative to total eIF2alpha; at least two independent transformants and SE are reported. Plate-growth conditions are separate.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figures 2 and 5C/D, main Methods and fragment Results; GST and total-eIF2alpha controls constrain the endpoint.
Exact reference mapping places this family in the ancient domain, not in the separate N-terminal RWD. Whole-protein effects cannot be assigned to PF01205 alone.

edges.mechanism: The overexpressed multidomain fusion decreases the normalized phosphorylation signal under the specified starvation treatment. Gcn2 regulation is the mechanistic interpretation, not a directly measured isolated-domain reaction in this assay.
edges.subject: overexpress-gst-yih1-h1511

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P25637/YIH1_YEAST is YCR059C, 258 aa, sequence version 1; the cited GI 6319904 resolves to matching NP_009985.1. PF01205 maps to 144-251 in the C-terminal ancient domain, despite the preserved Impact_N label. PF05773 RWD is separately at 6-108. The 2-258 fusion retains both; exact historical junctions remain unverified. P40512/PCI8 is an unrelated YIH1 synonym.
causal_graphs.limitations: Figure 2 confirms overexpression, not physiological dosage. RWD-only 2-132 lacks PF01205 yet inhibits, whereas 133-258 retains PF01205 but has little effect. This does not establish isolated PF01205 inhibition, direct eIF2alpha dephosphorylation or increased total translation. Binding and modeled actin switching are not an observed causal chain.

causal_graphs.scope: Saccharomyces cerevisiae H1511 expressing N-terminal GST-Yih1(2-258) from pES187-B1 versus GST alone in Sattlegger 2011 Figure 5C/D. This is a whole-protein overexpression phenotype.
causal_graphs.title: GST-Yih1 overexpression lowers starvation-induced eIF2alpha phosphorylation

causal_graphs.context: Spot 5 ul of tenfold serial dilutions of overnight cultures on synthetic minimal galactose medium with or without 3AT. The inspected 2011 caption does not specify plate 3AT concentration, incubation temperature or duration; the liquid 10-mM/1-h protocol is not transferred.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 5A with its nonstarved control, Figure 2 expression analysis, Methods/Table 1 and corresponding Results.

edges.mechanism: The full multidomain fusion reduces colony growth under the starvation challenge compared with GST alone. The effect is consistent with impaired starvation adaptation, without assigning direct toxicity or domain-local catalysis.
edges.subject: overexpress-yih1-wt-background

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The YCR059C fusion maps to P25637 with PF01205 at 144-251 and separate RWD at 6-108. Endogenous Yih1 remains present in this host. Current reference identity does not reconstruct every historical host or plasmid sequence.
causal_graphs.limitations: Growth is an indirect integrated phenotype, not direct kinase activity, viability loss or a quantified growth rate. Nonstarved plates constrain starvation specificity. This is not a normal-expression loss-of-function assay or an isolated ancient-domain effect.

causal_graphs.title: GST-Yih1 overexpression reduces H1511 growth under 3AT starvation

causal_graphs.context: The same 5-ul tenfold dilution plate assay uses galactose minimal medium with or without 3AT. Plate dose, time and temperature remain unverified; the deletion background is not combined with the H1511 phosphorylation assay.

evidence.explanation: Figure 5B was visually inspected separately from panel A; Methods identify ESY11001b as the H1511-derived yih1 deletion strain.

edges.mechanism: Expressing the multidomain fusion reduces the starvation-growth endpoint even when endogenous Yih1 is absent. This limits an endogenous-protein bridging explanation for this phenotype, but does not resolve the biochemical role of PF01205.
edges.subject: express-yih1-in-deletion-background

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The expressed P25637-mapped 2-258 fusion contains PF01205 144-251 and RWD 6-108. Endogenous YIH1 is deleted by the reported PCR-based construction; exact deletion junctions and fusion scars were not reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: This comparison shows that the overexpression-associated growth effect does not require endogenous Yih1. It is not rescue of a deletion defect. Figure 5B's truncated-construct labels differ from Table 1, but its adopted 2-258 row is unambiguous; those truncated rows are not new edges.

record.description: This entry represents the N-terminal domain of the Impact proteins. The Impact protein is a translational regulator that ensures constant high levels of translation under amino acid starvation. It acts by interacting with Gcn1/Gcn1L1, thereby preventing activation of Gcn2 protein kinases (EIF2AK1 to 4) and subsequent down-regulation of protein synthesis [[cite:PUB00161305],[cite:PUB00158485]]. It is evolutionary conserved from eukaryotes to archaea [[cite:PUB00046141]].

evidence.explanation: RWD-only fragments inhibit without PF01205, while the ancient-domain fragment is insufficient. Binding alone and modeled actin switching are not directed causal proof.
A later study reports Gcn1/Gcn2-independent cell-cycle effects requiring separate full-text and construct review.

discussions.notes: Preserve frozen identity metadata but investigate its N-terminal wording in the source-maintained workflow. Obtain exact fusion/host sequences and plate conditions; review 2004 competition, 2015 cell-cycle and mammalian studies separately. Do not generalize to bacterial YigZ or archaea. The PCI8/CSN11 YIH1 synonym is excluded. Partial same-agent scientific assessment; remain IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve the ancient-domain mechanism separately from RWD-driven Yih1 phenotypes.
discussions.rationale: PF01205 maps to C-terminal residues 144-251 despite the frozen Impact_N name. Three whole-protein phenotypes do not establish this domain's isolated mechanism.
